newsitem.title: USA: US spot prods down at close, diffs near steady.
newsitem.headline: US spot prods down at close, diffs near steady.

text.p: U.S. spot refined products prices slid lower Monday, led by the sharp drop in the NYMEX futures prices.

Spot activity was very thin Monday afternoon, with many brokers in Houston leaving their offices early to battles icy roads. A cold snap caused electrical outages that forced two links to the Colonial Pipeline to shut, though a pipeline spokesman said no reduction in line shipments occurred.
No refinery outages have been reported due to the cold blast, according to market watchers, since most of the plants are on the Gulf side of Houston, which was unaffected by ice.

U.S. Gulf conventional unleaded M4 gasoline diffs firmed about 0.25 cent early in the day, with offers for back 2nd cycle barrels on the Colonial Pipeline at 2.50 cents under NYMEX. However, those offers slipped back to about 2.75 cents under by mid-afternoon.
"There was a little spurt of action in the morning, but it really dried up later," one Gulf trader said.

In New York Harbor, prompt barrels of No. 2 oil were "well offered" at 0.50 cent above the screen, near even with late Friday levels. USG No. 2 oil barrels for the back 1st Colonial cycle were offered at 4.40 cents under the print.
On the NYMEX, market watchers pointed to the weakness in crude oil prices, as well as some weather reports calling for more moderate temperatures in the high-demand Northeast over the next week.
-- Matt Daily, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1626
